{{nihongo|'''Hayatani Shrine'''|速谷神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Kamihiraira, {{ill|Hatsukaichi|Q736897|qid=Q736897}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|Q617375|qid=Q617375}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), and the {{ill|Aki Province|Q965029|qid=Q965029}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Ninomiya}}. Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking}}, it was a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kokuhei Chūsha}}, and is now a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}. {{nihongo|'''Hayatani Shrine'''|速谷神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Aki Province]].

== Overview ==
A shrine enshrining the ancestral deity of the founding of {{ill|Aki Province|Q965029|qid=Q965029}}, and the general tutelary shrine of Aki Province. With a history of over 1,800 years, it was once considered of higher rank than {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|Q191763|qid=Q191763}}.

It is known nationwide as a shrine for prayers for {{ill|Road safety|Q1147899|qid=Q1147899}}, and many worshippers come from afar with the saying, “If you buy a car, go to Hayatani-san.” It is also famous for buses and trains of {{ill|Hiroshima Electric Railway|Q1196530|qid=Q1196530}} receiving purification rites.

Along with {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|Q191763|qid=Q191763}} and {{ill|Take Shrine|Q11430665|qid=Q11430665}}, it is one of the “Three Great Shrines of Aki Province.” Many traditions remain of travelers on the {{ill|San'yōdō|Q1376722|qid=Q1376722}} praying for safety on long journeys, and it is still revered as the “guardian deity of traffic safety” protecting the San'yōdō.

== Enshrined deity ==
* Akihayatamao-no-Mikoto
*: Said to be the fifth-generation descendant of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-Yuzuhiko-no-Mikoto}}, one of the 32 deities accompanying the {{ill|Tenson kōrin|Q1084733|qid=Q1084733}}.<ref>From the official website.</ref> Listed in the '{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|Q133833194|qid=Q133833194}}' as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aki no miyatsuko}}.<ref name=chimei>"Place Names of Hiroshima Prefecture," entry for Hayatani Shrine.</ref>

== History ==
Although the year of enshrinement is unclear, it is an ancient shrine with more than 1,800 years since founding, and is considered the oldest shrine in {{ill|Aki Province|Q965029|qid=Q965029}}.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://hayatanijinja.jp/img/taisainiyosete.pdf |title=From “The Oldest Shrine Transmitting the Earliest Aki” (Naoki Shintani) |access-date=2025-08-10}}</ref>

In the reign of {{ill|Emperor Saga|Q316654|qid=Q316654}}, in {{ill|Kōnin (era)|Q1373070|qid=Q1373070}} 2 ({{ill|811|Q29946|qid=Q29946}}), it was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964|lt=myōjin}} as recorded in the official history '{{ill|Nihon Kōki|Q1077029|qid=Q1077029}}'; this is the oldest record concerning a shrine in Hiroshima Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|title=“Chronology of Hiroshima Prefecture History,” from ancient times|url=https://www.pref.hiroshima.lg.jp/soshiki_file/monjokan/nenpyou/nenpyou-kodai.pdf|access-date=2025-09-01}}</ref>

In {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 1 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|qid=Q349243}}, its {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} was raised from Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade; in year 9 ({{ill|867|Q30347|qid=Q30347}}), it was further advanced to Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade.

In {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}} 5 ({{ill|905|Q24239|qid=Q24239}}), during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Daigo|Q329753|qid=Q329753}}, the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}' records “Saeki District, Aki Province: Hayatani Shrine, Myōjin Taisha, Tsukinami, Niiname,” listing it among the imperial-offering {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}} shrines. As a shrine for protection of the state, it received offerings from the {{ill|Department of Divinities|Q2264720|qid=Q2264720}} at the three annual rites: {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161}}, {{ill|Kinensai|Q118906710|qid=Q118906710}}, and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}}. In this way it was deeply revered by the court from ancient times, and in antiquity held the highest shrine rank not only in Aki and Bingo Provinces but among the eight provinces of the {{ill|San'yōdō|Q1376722|qid=Q1376722}}.

In {{ill|Jōhei|Q1324874|qid=Q1324874|lt=Jōhei}} 5 ({{ill|935|Q24867|qid=Q24867}}) during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Suzaku|Q361019|qid=Q361019}}, in the {{ill|Tengyō no Ran|Q2975322|qid=Q2975322|lt=Fujiwara no Sumitomo rebellion}}, the court prayed for pacification at thirteen shrines nationwide including Hayatani Shrine; when the disturbance was soon subdued, its {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} was raised to Senior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade.

It is said to have originally been the {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} of Aki Province, but as {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|Q191763|qid=Q191763}} came to be patronized by the {{ill|Taira clan|Q1079102|qid=Q1079102}}, it came to be called the Aki Province Ninomiya.<ref name=chimei/>

From the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}, successive lords including Fujiwara Chikazane and later castellans of {{ill|Sakurao Castle|Q11537973|qid=Q11537973}} in {{ill|Aki Province|Q965029|qid=Q965029}}, Sengoku daimyō such as {{ill|Ōuchi Yoshitaka|Q1065163|qid=Q1065163}} and {{ill|Mōri Motonari|Q1156545|qid=Q1156545}}, and later Hiroshima domain lords beginning with {{ill|Asano Mitsuakira|Q11557318|qid=Q11557318}} all deeply revered Hayatani Shrine, donating sacred treasures and shrine lands, and carrying out construction and repairs of the shrine buildings.

In {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 13 ({{ill|1924|Q2173|qid=Q2173}}), it was ranked as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kokuhei Chūsha}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine rank system}}. In {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 21 ({{ill|1946|Q18610|qid=Q18610}}), with abolition of the government system, it became a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} under the Association of Shinto Shrines.

== Court ranks ==
* {{ill|Kōnin (era)|Q1373070|qid=Q1373070}} 2 ({{ill|811|Q29946|qid=Q29946}}), {{ill|July 17|Q2729|qid=Q2729}}, listed as Myōjin ('Nihon Kōki') – written as “Hayatani no Kami.”
* {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} 3 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), {{ill|January 27|Q2284|qid=Q2284}}, from Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade ('Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') – written as “Hayatani no Kami.”
* {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 9 ({{ill|867|Q30347|qid=Q30347}}), {{ill|October 13|Q2925|qid=Q2925}}, Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade ('Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') – written as “Hayatani no Kami.”

== Affiliated and minor shrines ==
* Iwaki Shrine - Enshrined deity: Iwaki-Okina-no-Kami. Said to be a local deity from before the main shrine’s enshrinement, and there is a theory identifying it with “Ishiki Myōjin” recorded in the 'Aki no Kuni Jinmyōchō.'<ref name=chimei/>
* Inari Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|Ukanomitama|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Kami}}.
